title: Upgrade Communications & Release Notes Playbook for LTS Channels and Rollout Gates
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Playbook and set of customer-facing artifacts for announcing, documenting, and supporting upgrades to runtime-2.4-LTS and subsequent LTS branches. Covers versioning semantics, how LTS and patch channels are communicated, staged rollout gates, explicit migration steps for admin/API changes, in-product banners, changelog templates, status page language, and CSM+Support runbooks. Goal: reduce support load during LTS upgrades, make migration paths predictable, and ensure no-surprises for high-value customers.
acceptance_criteria: A single canonical changelog template exists that can be auto-populated from release notes and linked from the customer dashboard
Email + in-product banner + KB article templates approved by legal and support
Rollout plan with gates (0%, 5%, 25%, 60%, 100%) defined and automation hooks for abort/rollback tested in staging
Migration guide contains actionable CLI/API steps, sample requests, and a compatibility table; verified by Eng and SE
On-call and CSM runbook created with clear escalation paths and canned responses
comm_templates: Email subject: Important: Redwood runtime-2.4-LTS upgrade rolling out Feb 28 — action required only if you pin old versions

Email body: Hi {customer_name},

We're releasing runtime-2.4-LTS with stable performance and security patches. This release includes a minor API change to the routing header (X-Redwood-Routing -> X-RW-Routing). Customers who pin an exact runtime tag will not be auto-upgraded; customers on 'lts' channel will receive the update during the staged rollout window. No action required for most customers. If you patch-protect integrations or maintain on-prem bundles, please review the migration steps below.

Summary: performance improvements (~12% median latency), bugfixes for KV cache invalidation, and a small header rename.

Link to migration guide: {kb_url}
If you need assistance, contact support@redwood.ai or open a support ticket.

Thanks,
The Redwood Release Team
In-product banner (short): runtime-2.4-LTS is rolling out. Click to see changes and migration steps. Planned opt-in upgrade window: Feb 28 - Mar 3.

Status page update: Incident: Planned upgrade to runtime-2.4-LTS. Impact: None expected for unpinned customers; customers with strict pinning may need to update. Maintenance window: 2026-02-28 02:00-06:00 UTC. Follow progress: {status_page_link}

Slack DM to CSM team: Heads-up: LTS 2.4 rollout starts Feb 28. Key customers with pinning: AcmeCorp, Finlytics. See playbook: {confluence_link}. If customers report tokenization change regressions, escalate to ENG-8021.

KB article intro: This article explains what's in runtime-2.4-LTS, whether your project is affected, and step-by-step migration instructions for pinned/private deployments. For hosted customers on the 'lts' channel no action is required unless you rely on the old X-Redwood-Routing header.
changelog_summary: runtime-2.4-LTS: backported security + performance fixes from runtime-2.5 dev branch
Behavioral change: routing header renamed X-Redwood-Routing -> X-RW-Routing (backwards-compatible header accepted for 90 days)
KV cache fix: resolved edge-case where context-length>12k would drop cached prefixes
Performance: median token throughput improvement of 12% on A100 80GB for short queries
Bugfix: deterministic seed drift fixed for repeatable sampling endpoints
migration_guide_steps: 1) Identify if you pin a runtime tag: check dashboard > Settings > Model pins or query /v1/account/pins
2) If pinned to runtime-2.3.*: plan for upgrade to runtime-2.4-LTS. Test in a staging workspace by switching channel to 'lts-2.4-staging' for 24 hours
3) Update integrations that set routing header to accept X-RW-Routing or continue sending X-Redwood-Routing for backward compatibility during the 90-day grace period
4) Verify health: run the canonical smoke test collection (links in KB) and compare latency and output diffs using the provided eval harness

5) If you run Private (VPC) deployments: request the 2.4 OVA from your solutions engineer and follow the on-prem upgrade checklist (preflight, downtime windows, config migrations), then apply the patch bundle
6) For Dedicated customers with reserved pools: open a support ticket to schedule a maintenance window with the platform team to avoid autoscaler churn
7) If you observe regression, switch pin back to runtime-2.3.X immediately and contact support with the 'upgrade-regression' tag
rollback_plan: Immediate rollback: For hosted LTS, toggle the routing config to the previous runtime tag via admin console; this will revert runtime for affected pools within 2-5 minutes
Staged rollback: if aborting during a gate, halt further traffic promotion and revert newly promoted pools only
On-prem rollback: restore VM snapshot taken before upgrade and validate config; file support ticket for assistance
Communication: Notify customers within 30 minutes of rollback decision with reason and next steps using the incident template
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary): 0% -> 5% of traffic on non-critical pools for 1 hour to validate basic health checks
Phase 1: 5% -> 25% over 3 hours if health checks pass and no SLO alerts triggered
Phase 2: 25% -> 60% over 6 hours with targeted customer notifications to a short list of opt-in accounts
Phase 3: 60% -> 100% over 12 hours; full GA once final gate completes
Abort conditions evaluated at each gate: >2% increase in 5m error rate, >15% increase in median latency, scope-specific functional regression detected by eval harness
gating_criteria: Functional tests: canonical smoke suite passes in canary pools for 30m
Observability: no new P99 latency deviations beyond configured thresholds; token error rate < 0.5%
Customer reports: zero high-severity customer bugs within canary cohort
Manual sign-off: Release lead + On-call Eng + PM must approve before moving to next gate
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards to watch: runtime-latency-overview, kv-cache-errors, header-mismatch-rate, model-outputs-regression
Alerts: page if 5m error rate > 1% or P99 latency > baseline + 50% for 10m
Synthetic tests: run text-generation and embedding checks every minute against canary pools; alert on output-drift score > 0.06
Data retention for rollouts: snapshot token-level metrics and eval diffs for 30 days for postmortem
